knownGaps.evidence: completion-browser-session.jsonl: seq6 task-frame.goal holds the full human message; seq18 after native create_goal replaces it with the model-written objective and items=[]; completion reviews only receive that objective and no initial extra requirements.
knownGaps.scope: Initial additional human requirements can be absent from review, including allowed/forbidden tools, paths, dependencies, output and acceptance requirements. This is not limited to the five tools used by this scenario.
knownGaps.capacity: Messages longer than maxMessageChars are skipped by the task frame; additions beyond maxItems retain only the most recent items. Neither limit is a safety guarantee or proof that all human requirements are preserved.
knownGaps.nextAction: After design approval, preserve human instruction sources independently of model Goal objectives, then validate initial/appended requirements, explicit replacement/revocation, capacity overflow, reopen and covered execution paths with real E2E.

configurationAndLifecycleVerification.configurationDependency: An active/shadow completion review rejects taskFrame.mode=off at load; a missing taskFrame is rejected. Off review may use an off frame; shadow/active frames remain supported.
configurationAndLifecycleVerification.unload: Plugin unload aborts a pending review and delegates to remaining tool policies without refusing native completion or appending a late completion-review record. Caller cancellation still prevents execution; late provider answers after abort do not append a new judgement. A judgement committed before unload remains logged but its result is not applied after unload.
configurationAndLifecycleVerification.taskFrameUnload: Task-frame asynchronous work does not append a late frame after unload.
configurationAndLifecycleVerification.verificationOwner: coordinating agent; focused unit regression execution
configurationAndLifecycleVerification.limitation: These configuration/lifecycle mechanisms are deterministic focused regressions; the three fresh real scenarios validate normal active execution, not fault injection of every lifecycle path.
